Cincinnati River Bridges

The C&O and Cincinnati Southern Bridges

The two four-track Ohio River crossings drawn together on the canon ground, in their true positions about 2 km apart. Upstream, the C&O Bridge (about 1925-27): two Ludendorff-type truss arches side by side on shared river piers, with American trusses, its viaduct from the tunnel portals under W 6th and its Kentucky approach to Covington Union. Downstream, the Cincinnati Southern Bridge (about 1927-31): a Hell Gate-type spandrel-braced arch of 402.2 m between masonry towers, with RER C under the Embankment.

Against the Ludendorff Bridge, same scale

C&O (drawing)Ludendorff Bridge, Remagen

Ludendorff Bridge (1916-19): steel section 325.4 m, side spans 84.6 m (parallel-chord through trusses), two-hinged truss arch of 156.2 m rising 28.5 m above the deck, two river piers. Its truss depths and hinge level are not published; both outlines use this drawing's values.

Against Hell Gate and Sydney Harbour, same scale

Cincinnati Southern (drawing)Hell GateSydney Harbour

Hell Gate: 977.5 ft (297.9 m) clear between the towers, deck 145 ft (44 m) and upper chord about 305 ft (93 m) above mean high water, towers 220 ft (67 m). Sydney Harbour: 503 m span, arch top 134 m and deck 49 m above the water, truss 18 m deep at the crown and 57 m at the pylons, pylons 89 m. Both outlines come from those published figures; chord shapes, bearing levels and pylon widths are approximate. Heights are above each bridge's water level.
